answers.answer: Keep 4 tokens of each gem color and all 5 gold tokens. Reveal 3 nobles. Remove the other nobles from the game permanently.
answers.evidence: Token Adjustments: 2 players: 4 gems per color, 5 gold, 3 nobles. Setup: 'Remove remaining noble tiles from the game -- they will not be used.'

answers.answer: Three players use 5 gems per color, 5 gold and 4 nobles. Four players use 7 gems per color, 5 gold and 5 nobles: two more gems per color and one more noble, with gold unchanged.
answers.evidence: Token Adjustments by Player Count lists 3: 5 / 5 / 4 and 4: 7 / 5 / 5.

answers.answer: Shuffle the three level decks separately. Arrange them in a column with level 1 at bottom, level 2 in the middle and level 3 on top. Reveal four cards per level for a 3-by-4 market. The youngest player starts, and play goes clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–3; First Player: 'The youngest player goes first. Play proceeds clockwise.'

answers.answer: Choose exactly one: take three gems of different colors; take two gems of one color if at least four are in that supply; reserve one card with fewer than three already reserved and take one gold if available; or buy one face-up or previously reserved card. You cannot take gems then buy, or reserve then buy that card, on the same turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'must perform exactly one' of the four listed actions; purchasing includes a card 'reserved on a previous turn.'

answers.answer: All tokens you own must be visible to every player at all times.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: 'All tokens a player owns must be visible to all players at all times.'

answers.answer: You may take two green from four, leaving two. You may not take two red from three. Check the four-token threshold before taking the tokens. Neither gem-taking action allows gold.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'at least 4 tokens in the supply before taking them'; both gem-taking actions specify 'no gold.'

answers.answer: Temporarily holding twelve is allowed. Return two tokens of your choice to finish with ten; these may include tokens just drawn. Gold counts toward the limit.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit permits temporarily exceeding 10, requires returning tokens to exactly 10, includes gold, and allows returning newly taken tokens.

answers.answer: Take the gold, temporarily reaching eleven tokens, then return one token of your choice, including that gold if desired, to end with ten. If the gold supply is empty, you may still reserve, receive no gold and remain at ten tokens.
answers.evidence: Reserve: 'If no gold tokens remain, you may still reserve a card but receive no gold.' Token Hand Limit allows returning gold obtained by reserving.

answers.answer: Reserve either a face-up market card or the top card from any of the three level decks. A deck reservation is taken without showing opponents. Only the reserving player may buy it.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card lists face-up cards or 'The top card' of any level deck 'without revealing it'; reserved cards may only be purchased by their reserver.

answers.answer: You cannot reserve a fourth card, even just to get gold. You cannot discard or exchange a reserved card to make room; purchasing it is the only way it leaves your hand.
answers.evidence: Reserved Cards: 'Maximum of 3'; 'The only way to remove a reserved card from your hand is to purchase it.'

answers.answer: Immediately refill the reserved level-2 card's space with the top card of the level-2 deck. A face-up purchase uses the same immediate replacement rule. Buying a reserved card removes no market card, so creates no market space to refill. If the relevant deck is empty, an emptied market space remains empty for the rest of the game.
answers.evidence: Card Replacement: 'Whenever a face-up card is acquired (purchased) or reserved from the grid, it is immediately replaced' from the same level; an empty deck leaves the space empty.

answers.answer: Spend one green token; the two blue bonuses cover the blue cost. If bonuses cover every cost, spend no tokens. Bonuses are permanent and are not spent.
answers.evidence: Payment rules give this exact blue/green example, call bonuses permanent, and allow purchase 'without spending any tokens at all.'

answers.answer: Yes. Bonuses leave a cost of one blue, one black and one white. Pay the blue token for blue and one gold each for black and white. Return all three spent tokens to the supply. Your purchased bonus cards stay with you.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: bonuses reduce tokens spent; gold substitutes for any single gem; spent gems and gold return to supply. Bonus Stacking calls card bonuses permanent.

answers.answer: Buy a face-up market card or a card you reserved previously. Place purchased cards face-up in front of you, sorted by bonus color and staggered so everyone can always see their bonuses and prestige values.
answers.evidence: Purchase a Development Card specifies the two sources and says cards are 'sorted by bonus color and staggered so that bonuses and prestige point values are visible to all players at all times.'

answers.answer: You do not qualify with only two white bonuses; a white or gold token cannot replace the missing bonus. A third white bonus qualifies you at the end of your turn, assuming the noble is available. Bonuses above requirements are allowed.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits requires 'at least' the shown bonuses; Noble Tile Mechanics: 'bonuses ... not gem tokens' and 'having more is fine.'

answers.answer: Choose exactly one noble; you cannot take both or decline all visits. The visit does not use an action, gives three prestige points, and eligibility is checked at the end of your turn after your action.
answers.evidence: Noble visit rules: automatic, not an action, choose one of multiple nobles, at most one per turn, and each worth 3 points.

answers.answer: Place the noble tile face-up in front of you.
answers.evidence: Noble visit rules: 'Place the received noble tile face-up in front of you.'

answers.answer: C and D still take their turns, then the game ends. A does not take another turn, because everyone then has equal turn counts. B is not guaranteed to win; the highest final prestige total wins.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger completes the current round so everyone has the same number of turns; End-of-Game Clarifications says the triggering player may be surpassed.

answers.answer: Your total becomes sixteen. That triggers the end condition because it is fifteen or more, even though fifteen was skipped. Determine the winner after the current round finishes and all players have equal turn counts.
answers.evidence: Nobles are worth 3; End-Game Trigger: '15 or more'; Determining the Winner uses the most points 'at the end of the final round.'

answers.answer: B wins. A and B tie for highest prestige, and B has fewer purchased developments, nine versus ten. C's fifteen points lose despite fewer cards. Nobles count toward prestige. B's three reserved cards have not been purchased and do not count for this tiebreaker.
answers.evidence: Winner is most prestige; 'Noble tile points count'; tiebreaker is 'fewest development cards' purchased. Reserved cards must be purchased to leave the hand.

answers.answer: Unpurchased reserved cards contribute neither their eight printed points to your score or end trigger nor their two white bonuses to purchase discounts or nobles.
answers.evidence: Prestige Point Sources: points printed on each 'purchased card'; payment bonuses come from 'previously purchased development cards'; noble bonuses come from purchased cards.

answers.answer: You receive no physical blue token. The purchased card's blue bonus permanently reduces future blue purchase costs and can satisfy noble requirements even though the card is worth zero prestige.
answers.evidence: Bonus Stacking: 'Bonuses ... never generate tokens'; each purchased card adds one permanent bonus. Nobles require bonuses, with no prestige requirement stated.

answers.answer: The card cannot use its own bonus to make its purchase free; discounts come from previously purchased cards, so you cannot pay the blue cost. A newly purchased white bonus does count for a noble at the end of that same turn, because the noble check follows the action.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: 'previously purchased development cards'; Turn Structure: after the action, check hand limit and then noble visit.

answers.answer: Excess blue bonuses cannot pay green costs or produce blue tokens as change. The blue cost is covered, but you must still pay two green tokens or equivalent gold substitutes.
answers.evidence: Bonus Stacking: excess in a color provides 'no benefit for that purchase (no "change" is given)' and bonuses never generate tokens; gold substitutes for any gem.

answers.answer: The first noble does not use up your permanent bonuses. If the other noble remains available, taking gems next turn still allows receiving it at that turn's end. You cannot receive it during an opponent's intervening turn; your noble check is at the end of your own turn.
answers.evidence: Bonuses are permanent; Noble Visits: 'At the end of their turn' and other qualifying nobles 'remain available for future turns.'

answers.answer: Yes, you may reserve that level-3 card despite being unable to buy it. Reserving takes the card without paying its printed purchase cost, and gives one gold if available. You have room under the three-card reservation limit.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card allows one face-up development or top card of any level and awards one gold; payment of printed cost appears under the separate Purchase action.

answers.answer: No market card is removed or refilled. All twelve market cards remain. You take only the single reserved top card, with no second card as a replacement in your hand.
answers.evidence: Reserve says 'Take one development card' and permits a top-deck card. Replacement applies when a face-up card is purchased or reserved 'from the grid.'

answers.answer: The four face-up cards stay available for purchase or reservation. Purchasing one leaves its space empty permanently because the deck is exhausted; the other three remain available.
answers.evidence: Purchase and Reserve allow face-up cards; Card Replacement: 'If the corresponding deck is empty, the empty space ... remains empty for the rest of the game.'

answers.answer: Exhaustion does not end the game. The player may buy the affordable reserved card or choose the three-different-gems action, since those legal actions remain available. Continue until the prestige end condition.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: 'Exhausting the development decks or the face-up market does not end the game. Continue with the remaining legal actions, including purchasing reserved cards.'

answers.answer: Yes. Take one gem from each of three different colors, temporarily hold thirteen, then return all three newly taken gems to end with the same ten tokens. No net token gain is required.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: a player may temporarily exceed 10 and 'may return some or all of the tokens they just took.'

answers.answer: A's two spent gold tokens return to the supply. B takes one when reserving, leaving one gold in the supply immediately afterward, before any token-limit returns.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: 'Spent gold tokens are returned to the supply'; reserving takes '1 gold token' if available.

answers.answer: Yes. If you can pay, you may purchase a face-up level-3 card immediately; the purchase rule does not require buying lower-level cards first.
answers.evidence: Purchase a Development Card: 'Purchase a face-up development card from the grid ... by paying the gem token cost shown on the card.' No level prerequisite is imposed.

answers.answer: You cannot skip the automatic noble visit. Your turn ends with eighteen prestige: twelve plus three from the card plus three from the noble. Other players who still have a turn in the current round continue playing before the winner is determined.
answers.evidence: Noble visit is 'automatic' and 'cannot refuse'; nobles worth 3; reaching '15 or more' completes the current round.

answers.answer: The game ends after D completes the turn. A does not start another round and nobody gets an extra turn, because A, B, C and D have already taken equal numbers of turns when D finishes the current round.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: complete 'the current round' so every player has played 'the same number of turns.'

answers.answer: Do not reveal a replacement. The seven removed nobles are permanently out of the game. Put the acquired noble face-up in front of its recipient, leaving two available nobles in the middle.
answers.evidence: Noble Tile Mechanics: tiles removed during setup are 'out of the game permanently'; received nobles go 'face-up in front of you.'

answers.answer: Emerald is green, diamond white, sapphire blue, onyx black, ruby red, and gold joker yellow. There are ninety development cards: forty level 1, thirty level 2 and twenty level 3.
answers.evidence: Components token-color table and Development Cards table: 90 total, with levels 1/2/3 containing 40/30/20.

answers.answer: You may pay the gold and keep your green token. Gold may substitute for any single gem token; the payment goes back to the supply.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: 'Gold tokens (jokers) can substitute for any single gem token. Spent gold tokens are returned to the supply.'

answers.answer: Yes, take one red, one blue and one green. The four-token minimum applies only to taking two of the same color. The piles then contain zero red, one blue and two green.
answers.evidence: Take 3 Gem Tokens: 'Take 1 gem token from each of 3 different color piles'; the four-token threshold is specified for 'Take 2 Gem Tokens of the Same Color.'

answers.answer: A direct gold-for-red exchange without buying a card is not one of the four listed actions and is not the purchasing substitution described. Gold substitutes for a gem token when paying to purchase a development card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure requires exactly one of four actions and lists no exchange action. Gold Token Specifics: gold substitutes for any gem color 'when purchasing a card.'

answers.answer: You must choose and perform one of the four actions. Voluntarily passing with legal actions available is not permitted.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'On their turn, a player must perform exactly one of the following four actions.'
